summary: Frontend-only verification of the 3-pronged landing-hero timelapse performance fix (prefetch + localStorage cache + animated fallback bloom). All three mechanisms are correctly wired and functional. All 4 regression checks pass. Actual first-paint timings are still dominated by cold tunnel + JS bundle parse; cache-hit paint is measurable improvement but not the promised sub-500ms.

integration_issues.flow: Landing hero timelapse — cache-hit paint timing
integration_issues.issue: Second-visit paint (with valid localStorage cache) measured at ~12.6s to timelapse-stamp attachment; documented target is <500ms / <1s. The React Query useMapTimelapse `initialData: readTimelapseCache` is correctly reading the cache (verified: cache has {ts, data.frames[43]} and content renders correctly from it), but time-to-first-paint is dominated by CRA dev-bundle download+parse (deck.gl + react-query on this preview host) — the cache saves the network round-trip but not the bundle cost. First-ever cold visit measured at ~25.4s to paint (which is within the 30-90s cold-tunnel expectation). The improvement (cache vs cold: ~50%) is real but not the promised order-of-magnitude jump.

Fresh visit fires 3 requests to /v1/map/timelapse (all identical params, all resource_type=fetch). Expected 1 (prefetch consumed by React). Likely causes: React StrictMode double-mount of AmbientHeat before the promise-consumption short-circuit takes effect, plus possibly a background refetch. Not user-visible but wastes tunnel capacity.

verifications_passed.R2_settle_animation_working: AmbientHeat inner wrapper transform = matrix(1,0,0,1,211.2,0) i.e. 11% translateX after 700ms
verifications_passed.R4_malformed_cache_does_not_crash: landing-page renders, no console errors, no error DOM nodes

timings_ms.note: Fresh cold-tunnel budget documented as 30-90s; cache-hit target documented as <500ms — not met, dominated by bundle parse in this dev preview

action_items: Investigate why cache-hit visit takes ~12s to first paint despite `initialData` being available synchronously in useMapTimelapse. Suspects: (a) `enabled: Boolean(apiKey)` — TierContext may resolve apiKey asynchronously, delaying initialData surface; (b) CRA dev-server bundle is not code-split so the entire deck.gl + heatmap payload must parse before AmbientHeat mounts. Consider code-splitting DeckGL/HeatmapLayer via React.lazy so the watermark can render from cache without waiting for the aggregation-layers bundle.
Optional: dedupe the fresh-visit /v1/map/timelapse request count (3 → 1). Consider whether React StrictMode double-effect is causing the second/third fetch after the prefetch is consumed.

index.css hero-drift keyframes respect prefers-reduced-motion — verified in code.
